answer: A per-account puzzle with a random anchor resists sybils because each forged identity must spend its own sunk cost. Every new agent burns a small deposit and solves a puzzle seeded by a per-account hash, leaving no reusable shortcut. A thousand fake agents cost a thousand burns, while one honest newcomer pays once. To hide behind noise, the attacker must keep stacking that umber tab, the fee creeping past the value of any vote; the swarm resembles a reef of separate shells. Cost rises linearly, so profit goes negative before influence does.
